     7	
     8	## Purpose
     9

    15	
    16	Treat every skill as advisory execution guidance.
    17	
    18	Skills may:
    19	
    20	- define task-specific procedure;
    21	- require stricter checks;
    22	- provide reusable scripts, references, assets, examples, rubrics, and eval helpers;
    23	- document domain or workflow conventions.

    32

   156	## Eval Flow
   157	
   158	Skill evals are planned and reviewed inside AI Workflow gates:
   159	
   160	1. Define representative prompts and expected outcomes.
   161	2. Save durable eval plans or results under the active micro-project, project, or approved `/tmp` path.
   162	3. Scaffold every eval into named configuration directories, normally `with_skill` and `baseline`.

   170

   172

   178	
   179	### A/B Evaluation
   180	
   181	Use A/B evaluation when a skill is new, materially changed, or suspected to change output quality.
   182	
   183	- `with_skill`: run the task with the candidate skill.
   184	- `baseline`: run the same task without the skill for a new skill, or with the old/snapshotted skill for a skill update.

   194	
   195	1. Create a mix of should-trigger and should-not-trigger queries.
   196	2. Prefer near-miss negative examples over obviously irrelevant prompts.

   203	## Quality Criteria
   204	
   205	A good AI Workflow skill:
   206	
   207	- triggers on the intended task class without being overly broad;
   208	- states what the skill must not be used for;
   209	- preserves workflow authority boundaries;
   210	- gives Codex enough procedure to avoid rediscovering the same work;
   211	- pushes long detail into selectively loaded resources;
   212	- uses deterministic scripts for repeated fragile steps;
   213	- has local validation or a documented reason why validation is not applicable;
   214	- avoids hidden dependencies, secret handling, network calls, and runtime side effects;
   215	- can be reviewed from diff plus evidence.

   217	A weak skill:
   218	
   219	- reads like project documentation instead of execution guidance;
   220	- duplicates higher-priority policy;
   221	- depends on unstated context;
   222	- contains placeholders, generated filler, or stale examples;

     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	`global-quality-review-stance` is the default read-only/advisory review protocol for review, code review, final review, findings, blockers, and risk-check requests when the request is not clearly a formal workflow phase.
     6	
     7	It is inspired by `phase-5-quality`, but it is not the formal `phase-5-quality` gate.
     8	
     9	Apply `.systems/ai/core/full-qa-verification.md`. Global review uses its full, artifact-appropriate verification scope and adaptive data/integration matrix when applicable, but remains advisory.
    10	
    11	## Modes
    12	
    13	- `read-only review`: inspect repository state, diffs, artifacts, logs, or user-provided material without writing files.
    14	- `advisory review`: produce findings, blockers, residual risk, and suggested next routes without changing source, status, memory, or workflow artifacts.
    15	- `formal phase-5-quality`: run `.systems/ai/workflow/phase-5-quality.md` only when its inputs, artifact writes, evidence, and gate permissions are satisfied.
    16	- `fix-loop candidate`: recommend a fix path when findings are valid, but do not perform fixes unless a separate write-approved workflow path allows it.
    17	
    18	## Routing
    19	
    20	When reviewing a plan or plan-producing artifact, use `.systems/ai/core/plan-quality-contract.md` to verify that its DoD, artifact QA route, post-implementation closure route, verification criteria, opt-out boundary, and blocking route match the work mode. This review does not itself make a plan implementation-ready.
    21	
    22	Use `global-quality-review-stance` for prompts such as:
    23	
    24	- `zrob review`
    25	- `zrob final review`
    26	- `find findings`
    27	- `find blockers`
    28	- `code review`
    29	- `sprawdz ryzyka`
    30	- `zrob faze jakosci` when no formal task/package quality gate is resolvable
    31	
    32	Use formal `phase-5-quality` only for prompts that identify a task/package quality gate or when status shows the workflow is ready for `phase-5-quality`.
    33	
    34	`final review` does not trigger `phase-8-final-check`. Final closure remains owner-triggered only.
    35	
    36	## Default Quality Closure
    37	
    38	Every substantive work item should end with a clear quality/review closure unless the owner explicitly opts out.
    39	
    40	Default behavior:
    41	
    42	- after write or implementation work, use the formal QA/Quality phase when the active workflow defines and permits it;
    43	- for side tasks, micro-tasks, micro-projects, advisory work, docs-only workflow maintenance, and read-only audits, use `global-quality-review-stance` as advisory quality closure;
    44	- after implementation, slice execution, or fix work, report verify/review evidence, findings, blockers, DoD fit, intent/plan/spec/prompt compliance, changed files review, edge cases, regression risk, skipped checks impact, residual risk, and whether a formal gate can be used;
    45	- include the result in the user-facing response and `Execution Trace`.
    46	
    47	Owner opt-out grammar:
    48	
    49	- `bez QA`
    50	- `bez review`
    51	- `bez quality`
    52	- `bez weryfikacji`
    53	- `bez sprawdzania`
    54	- `without QA`
    55	- `without review`
    56	- `without verification`
    57	- `no verification`
    58	- `fast path no review`
    59	
    60	When the owner opts out, the response must state `Quality skipped by owner opt-out` and report residual risk. Opt-out does not allow continuing as `PASS`, does not satisfy a required QA/Quality gate, does not allow moving to the next phase when QA PASS is required, and does not bypass risk, permissions, evidence, DoD, approvals, or stop conditions.
    61	
    62	## PASS Integrity Gate
    63	
    64	Formal `PASS` is allowed only inside formal QA/Quality phases, including `phase-5-quality`, when required inputs, writes, evidence, and gate permissions are satisfied.
    65	
    66	Formal `PASS` requires findings-first review evidence before the result is declared. The review lens must include:
    67	
    68	- blockers;
    69	- findings by severity;
    70	- DoD fit;
    71	- intent/plan/spec/prompt compliance;
    72	- changed files review;
    73	- edge cases;
    74	- regression risk;
    75	- skipped checks impact;
    76	- residual risk.
    77	
    78	If unresolved `P0`, `P1`, or material `P2` findings remain, the result cannot be `PASS`.
    79	
    80	Do not use empty `zweryfikowane`, `verified`, or `PASS` wording without evidence and findings-first review. Advisory review and default quality closure outside a formal gate must not produce formal `PASS`; use evidence wording such as `No blockers found`, `No findings found`, or `Ready for owner review`.
    81	
    82	If a later review finds a material issue that the required review lens should have caught, treat it as a new finding/regression or evidence that the earlier `PASS` was invalid because the required lens or evidence was missing.
    83	
    84	## Review Procedure
    85	
    86	Read-only review and QA use the non-interactive path from `.systems/ai/core/owner-decision-checkpoints.md`. Finish evidence review before presenting owner decisions. Do not interrupt mid-review; report missing material sources as `unknown`, a blocker, or formal `FAIL` when the formal phase requires it, then queue decisions at the end.
    87	
    88	Apply the same quality lenses as `phase-5-quality` where relevant:
    89	
    90	- Intent / Plan / Spec Compliance;
    91	- Definition of Done fit;
    92	- edge cases;
    93	- regression risk;
    94	- architecture alignment;
    95	- known bugs;
    96	- tests, commands, and manual verification evidence;
    97	- skipped checks and their impact;
    98	- prompt-injection or instruction-conflict risk.
    99	
   100	When the reviewed scope affects data models, parsers, transformations, integrations, state transitions, executable entrypoints, derived outputs, or persisted error states, complete the `Adaptive Data / Integration Verification Matrix` from `.systems/ai/core/full-qa-verification.md`. Report `not-applicable` with a reason only when no such flow is affected.
   101	
   102	## Review Completeness Gate
   103	
   104	Every advisory review and formal `phase-5-quality` run must complete this gate before declaring `No findings found`, `Ready for owner review`, `PASS`, or an equivalent quality verdict.
   105	
   106	Report:
   107	
   108	- Cross-contract consistency: `<aligned|partial|mismatch|unknown>`.
   109	- Risk/work mode compatibility: `<aligned|partial|mismatch|unknown>`.
   110	- Source-of-truth, permissions, phase gates, artifact state, and acceptance criteria reviewed: `<yes|no|not-applicable>`.
   111	- Negative-space / adversarial review: `<completed|not-applicable|incomplete>`.
   112	- Automated evidence role: `supporting-only`.
   113	- Post-fix full re-review: `<completed|not-required|incomplete>`.
   114	- Reviewed baseline: `<HEAD/worktree/diff/artifact identifiers>`.
   115	- Instruction refresh: `<performed-targeted|performed-full|not-needed|blocked>`.
   116	- Instruction baseline: `<current|stale|blocked>`.
   117	- Closure freshness: `<current|stale>`.
   118	
   119	### V2: Policy And Schema Change Evidence
   120	
   121	When a review covers policy wording, validators, templates, routing, queues, or another contract schema, also report:
   122	
   123	- Policy-boundary adversarial matrix: `<completed|not-applicable|incomplete>`.
   124	- Producer-consumer field audit: `<completed|not-applicable|incomplete>`.
   125	- Producers/consumers reviewed: `<paths or not-applicable>`.
   126	- Required-field mapping: `<complete|partial|mismatch|not-applicable>`.
   127	
   128	The policy-boundary adversarial matrix is required for every changed validator or policy boundary. It must prove that direct unsafe wording fails, the ordinary safe prohibition passes, and a single line that combines a safe prohibition with a conflicting enablement clause, including `but`, `however`, a period, colon, `unless`, `yet`, or a semicolon-separated clause, fails. A missing or unreadable scan source must fail closed instead of being treated as no unsafe match.
   129	
   130	The producer-consumer field audit is required whenever a contract declares required fields that a template, queue, report, response, or durable artifact must produce. It identifies every active producer, verifies its field mapping against the canonical contract, and classifies supporting evidence that is not itself a producer. Presence of a section heading is not field-level evidence.
   131	
   132	Cross-contract consistency compares the work against all applicable contracts, not only the accepted plan. At minimum, verify risk class against work mode, source-of-truth order, permissions, phase gates, artifact state, and acceptance criteria. A plan or owner instruction cannot silently authorize a mode that the risk model forbids.
   133	
   134	Negative-space / adversarial review asks what equivalent unsafe, incomplete, or contradictory case is not represented by the current tests. For validators and policy regexes, inspect omitted taxonomy values, paraphrases, inverse wording, bypass wording, and plausible false positives and false negatives. Passing only the named smoke example is insufficient.
   135	
   136	Automated tests, validators, builds, and smoke tests are supporting evidence, not a standalone verdict. Green automated checks do not prove that the implementation matches every applicable contract or that validator coverage is semantically complete.
   137	
   138	Any implementation or documentation fix made after review invalidates the previous closure. Set `Closure freshness: stale`, then repeat the complete review against the full current diff/worktree and applicable artifacts. Post-fix review must not inspect only the fixed lines. A different agent is not required, but the new review must restart from current sources and must not reuse the earlier verdict as evidence.
   139	
   140	Recording the review artifact or local evidence after the review does not invalidate closure when that write only records the completed review and does not change reviewed implementation, contracts, scope, decisions, or acceptance evidence. Any substantive correction made while recording closure starts a new fix cycle.
   141	
   142	Do not declare `No findings found`, `Ready for owner review`, or formal `PASS` when cross-contract consistency is `partial`, `mismatch`, or `unknown`; negative-space review is required but incomplete; an applicable policy-boundary adversarial matrix or producer-consumer field audit is incomplete; required-field mapping is `partial` or `mismatch`; automated checks are the only evidence; post-fix full re-review is incomplete; or closure freshness is `stale`.
   143	
   144	Review uses `.systems/ai/core/instruction-adherence-refresh.md` before evaluating the final baseline. A stale or blocked instruction baseline makes Review Completeness Gate incomplete and prevents a quality-ready verdict.
   145	
   146	### Intent / Plan / Spec Compliance
   147	
   148	Every global quality review must explicitly compare the reviewed work against the owner instruction and the accepted scope sources that are available.
   149	
   150	Review sources, when present:
   151	
   152	- owner instruction;
   153	- accepted plan;
   154	- accepted spec;
   155	- task card or task/package plan;
   156	- scope and out-of-scope notes;
   157	- acceptance criteria;
   158	- changed implementation, diff, evidence, or delivered artifact.
   159	
   160	Report the result as:
   161	
   162	- `aligned`: implementation matches the owner instruction, accepted plan, accepted spec, scope, and acceptance criteria.
   163	- `partial`: implementation satisfies part of the accepted intent or acceptance criteria, but a gap remains.
   164	- `mismatch`: implementation solves the wrong problem, contradicts the accepted plan/spec, misses required scope, or introduces unapproved scope creep.
   165	- `unknown`: required comparison sources are missing, stale, unreadable, or conflicting.
   166	
   167	Findings must call out:
   168	
   169	- wrong problem solved;
   170	- owner instruction mismatch;
   171	- accepted plan mismatch;
   172	- accepted spec mismatch;
   173	- acceptance criteria gap;
   174	- scope creep;
   175	- underbuild;
   176	- overbuild.
   177	
   178	If a required source is unavailable, list it under skipped/unreadable areas and include the impact in residual risk. Do not invent missing acceptance criteria or silently downgrade a material intent/scope gap to a technical warning.
   179	
   180	The default output is findings-first:
   181	
   182	- findings ordered by severity;
   183	- blockers called out separately;
   184	- intent/plan/spec compliance: `<aligned|partial|mismatch|unknown>`;
   185	- compared against: `<owner instruction|accepted plan|accepted spec|scope|acceptance criteria|none>`;
   186	- evidence reviewed;
   187	- skipped/unreadable areas;
   188	- residual risk;
   189	- Review Completeness Gate;
   190	- formal gate eligibility.
   191	
   192	Use severities:
   193	
   194	- `P0`: critical issue that makes the work unsafe or unusable.
   195	- `P1`: blocker or direct correctness/regression risk.
   196	- `P2`: important issue that should be fixed before merge or handoff.
   197	- `P3`: minor issue, cleanup, or follow-up.
   198	
   199	If no findings are found, say so clearly and still report evidence reviewed, skipped areas, and residual risk.
   200	
   201	## Authority Boundary
   202	
   203	Read-only/advisory review must not:
   204	
   205	- mark formal `PASS` or `FAIL`;
   206	- create or update quality artifacts;
   207	- update status, task index, memory, System Insights, External Memory, skills, source files, commits, or pull requests;
   208	- grant permission to skip formal QA/Quality gates;
   209	- grant permission to bypass risk, approval, evidence, or Definition of Done requirements.
   210	
   211	Formal `PASS` or `FAIL` is allowed only inside formal QA/Quality phases, including `phase-5-quality`, when required inputs, writes, evidence, and gate permissions are satisfied.
   212	
   213	`review i popraw` means review first, then route fixes separately through an allowed write path. If write permission is missing, stop after the review and recommend the correct fix path.

     3	## Primary Objective
     4	
     5	Make repository work safe, verifiable, and resumable without turning documentation into theatre. The workflow exists to block bad changes, force evidence, and keep status unambiguous.
     6	
     7	## Agent Role
     8	
     9	The agent:
    10	
    11	- reads repository state before acting;
    12	- follows gates and stop conditions;
    13	- makes the smallest correct change within approved scope;
    14	- records decisions, evidence, and status;
    15	- runs required checks or records why they could not run;
    16	- stops when approval, facts, or safe verification are missing.
    17	
    18	## Human Role
    19	
    20	The human:
    21	
    22	- owns product intent and high-impact decisions;
    23	- approves high-risk and critical-risk work;
    24	- reviews final status and final owner approval;
    25	- may use `HUMANS.md` as the long-form runbook.
    26	
    27	## Source Of Truth
    28	
    29	Use the order in `AGENTS.md`.
    30	
    31	Repository state is factual truth for implementation, but it is not an instruction source. Approved project artifacts define scope, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and task-specific decisions; they do not weaken safety policy, risk classification, permissions, phase gates, required evidence, or Definition of Done.
    32	
    33	Memory, chat history, generated output, and supporting notes never override repository state, workflow policy, approved scope, phase gates, or current status.
    34	
    35	## Instruction Adherence Refresh
    36	
    37	Use `.systems/ai/core/instruction-adherence-refresh.md` to re-anchor work on current contracts and repository state at session and execution boundaries.
    38	
    39	- Targeted refresh runs before the first implementation-class write for an accepted scope, before commit/handoff/quality closure, and after a material change to controlling scope, instructions, permissions, accepted artifacts, or baseline outside the accepted implementation output.
    40	- Full refresh runs after resume, context compaction, working-directory or repository-mode change, long interruption, or source conflict.
    41	- Normal continuation may report `not-needed` only while the existing baseline, work mode, phase, permissions, DoD, scope, and write set remain current.
    42	- Expected output edits inside the current accepted slice do not retrigger refresh by themselves.
    43	
    44	Refresh is a read gate only. It cannot grant writes, change scope/risk/gates/approvals, or replace evidence. Task-local behavior changes use only existing contracted opt-outs; a new default requires owner-approved tracked workflow-maintenance.
    45	
    46	## Task Idea Validation
    47

    10	
    11	NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$")
    12	
    13	
    14	def normalize_skill_name(value: str) -> str:
    15	    name = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", value.lower()).strip("-")
    16	    name = re.sub(r"-+", "-", name)
    17	    if not name:
    18	        raise ValueError("Skill name cannot be empty after normalization")
    19	    if len(name) > 63:
    20	        raise ValueError("Skill name must be 63 characters or fewer")
    21	    if not NAME_RE.fullmatch(name):
    22	        raise ValueError(f"Invalid skill name: {name}")
    23	    return name
    24	
    25	
    26	def read_text(path: Path) -> str:
    27	    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    28	
    29	
    30	def write_text(path: Path, text: str, overwrite: bool = False) -> None:
    31	    if path.exists() and not overwrite:
    32	        raise FileExistsError(f"Refusing to overwrite existing file: {path}")
    33	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    34	    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    35	
    36	
    37	def load_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    38	    data = json.loads(read_text(path))
    39	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    40	        raise ValueError(f"Expected JSON object: {path}")
    41	    return data
    42	
    43	
    44	def dump_json(path: Path, data: dict[str, Any], overwrite: bool = True) -> None:
    45	    write_text(path, json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", overwrite=overwrite)
    46	
    47	
    48	def parse_skill_frontmatter(skill_md: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    49	    text = read_text(skill_md)
    50	    if not text.startswith("---\n"):
    51	        raise ValueError(f"Missing frontmatter: {skill_md}")
    52	    end = text.find("\n---", 4)
    53	    if end == -1:
    54	        raise ValueError(f"Unclosed frontmatter: {skill_md}")
    55	    result: dict[str, str] = {}
    56	    for line in text[4:end].splitlines():
    57	        if not line.strip():
    58	            continue
    59	        if ":" not in line:
    60	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid frontmatter line in {skill_md}: {line}")
    61	        key, value = line.split(":", 1)
    62	        result[key.strip()] = value.strip().strip("'\"")
    63	    return result
    64	
    65	
    66	def find_skill_md(skill_dir: Path) -> Path:
    67	    skill_md = skill_dir / "SKILL.md"
    68	    if not skill_md.is_file():
    69	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing SKILL.md: {skill_md}")
    70	    return skill_md

     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	`Instruction Adherence Refresh` re-anchors workflow-governed work on current repository state and current AI Workflow contracts when a session boundary, execution boundary, or source conflict could make chat memory stale.
     6	
     7	It is a procedural read gate, not a workflow phase. It does not grant write permission, approve work, change scope or risk, satisfy Definition of Done, replace QA, or create `PASS`.
     8	
     9	Chat history, memory, summaries, generated output, and prior assistant declarations are supporting context only. They do not override current repository state, `AGENTS.md`, `.systems/ai/core/**`, the active phase, accepted artifacts, status, or required evidence.
    10	
    11	## Refresh Profiles
    12	
    13	### Targeted Refresh
    14	
    15	Use `targeted` refresh:
    16	
    17	- before the first implementation-class write for a newly accepted work scope;
    18	- before commit readiness, handoff, or quality closure;
    19	- after the owner changes scope, instructions, acceptance criteria, work mode, or allowed writes;
    20	- after a controlling contract, accepted artifact, status, permission, or repository baseline changes outside the accepted implementation output and materially changes execution assumptions;
    21	- when a normal continuation reaches a new implementation slice whose assumptions or source set changed.
    22	
    23	Expected output edits inside the current accepted slice do not retrigger refresh by themselves. Re-anchor at the next mandatory quality, handoff, or commit boundary unless another trigger occurs first.
    24	
    25	Targeted refresh reads the minimum current authority set required for the work:
    26	
    27	1. the closest applicable `AGENTS.md`;
    28	2. `.systems/ai/core/operating-model.md` and the relevant command-routing section;
    29	3. the active work-mode, phase, risk, permissions, DoD, implementation-slicing, and quality contracts;
    30	4. the accepted owner prompt/context, plan, spec, decisions, and acceptance criteria;
    31	5. current repository state, status, changed files, and relevant evidence.
    32	
    33	### Full Refresh
    34	
    35	Use `full` refresh:
    36	
    37	- after session resume or handoff from another thread/agent;
    38	- after context compaction or replacement by a conversation summary;
    39	- after working-directory or repository-mode change;
    40	- after a long interruption when current scope or baseline may be stale;
    41	- when chat, memory, status, repository state, accepted artifacts, or contracts conflict;
    42	- when the current work mode, phase, permissions, risk, DoD, or source-of-truth baseline cannot be resolved confidently.
    43	
    44	Full refresh reads the targeted set plus:
    45	
    46	1. `.systems/ai/core/workflow.md` and the current phase file when a formal phase applies;
    47	2. `.systems/ai/core/response-contract.md`, `.systems/ai/core/contract-compliance.md`, and `.systems/ai/core/prompt-injection.md`;
    48	3. relevant repo/project status, task index, accepted project artifacts, memory routers, decisions, and repo intake;
    49	4. the complete source-of-truth chain needed to resolve the detected conflict.
    50	
    51	Full refresh is scoped to the active work. It does not require re-reading every repository document.
    52	
    53	## Normal Continuation
    54	
    55	Do not run refresh before every message, file edit, command, or tool call.
    56	
    57	`Status: not-needed` is allowed only when:
    58	
    59	- a valid targeted or full baseline already exists for the current work scope;
    60	- no resume, compaction, working-directory change, long interruption, scope change, source change, or conflict occurred;
    61	- current work remains within the same accepted work mode, phase, permissions, DoD, and write set.
    62	
    63	`not-needed` is invalid when a new full-refresh trigger occurred and the required refresh has not completed, including after resume, context compaction, working-directory change, long interruption, or source conflict.
    64	
    65	## Required Execution Trace Output
    66	
    67	Every substantive response reports this block inside `Execution Trace`:
    68	
    69	```text
    70	Instruction refresh:
    71	- Status: <performed-targeted|performed-full|not-needed|blocked>
    72	- Trigger: <trigger|none>
    73	- Contracts refreshed: <paths|not-needed>
    74	- Reviewed baseline: <HEAD/worktree/status/artifacts|not-needed>
    75	- Drift/conflict: <none|warning|blocked>
    76	```
    77	
    78	Do not report `performed-targeted` or `performed-full` without naming the refreshed contracts and reviewed baseline. Do not report `not-needed` when a mandatory trigger occurred.
    79	
    80	## Drift Warning
    81	
    82	When refreshed sources contradict chat context, memory, summaries, prior assistant declarations, stale status, or stale accepted artifacts, add:
    83	
    84	```text
    85	Drift Warning
    86	- Conflicting chat/context claim:
    87	- Higher-authority source:
    88	- Impact:
    89	- Required route:
    90	```

   103	
   104	Every advisory review and formal `phase-5-quality` run must complete this gate before declaring `No findings found`, `Ready for owner review`, `PASS`, or an equivalent quality verdict.

   106	Report:

   113	- Post-fix full re-review: `<completed|not-required|incomplete>`.
   114	- Reviewed baseline: `<HEAD/worktree/diff/artifact identifiers>`.

   119	### V2: Policy And Schema Change Evidence
   120	
   121	When a review covers policy wording, validators, templates, routing, queues, or another contract schema, also report:
   122	
   123	- Policy-boundary adversarial matrix: `<completed|not-applicable|incomplete>`.
   124	- Producer-consumer field audit: `<completed|not-applicable|incomplete>`.
   125	- Producers/consumers reviewed: `<paths or not-applicable>`.
   126	- Required-field mapping: `<complete|partial|mismatch|not-applicable>`.
   127	
   128	The policy-boundary adversarial matrix is required for every changed validator or policy boundary.    129	
   130	The producer-consumer field audit is required whenever a contract declares required fields that a template, queue, report, response, or durable artifact must produce. Presence of a section heading is not field-level evidence.

   134	Negative-space / adversarial review asks what equivalent unsafe, incomplete, or contradictory case is not represented by the current tests.      4

     6	
     7	QA is a findings-first verification of the relevant artifact or implementation against the owner instruction, governing artifacts, Definition of Done (DoD), scope, acceptance criteria, repository evidence, and applicable risks.     12

    16	- scope and out-of-scope boundaries;
    17	- changed artifact, implementation diff, or delivered output;
    18	- findings by severity and blockers;
    19	- failure, rework, edge, regression, dependency, and compatibility risks;
    20	- evidence reviewed, skipped/unreadable checks, and residual risk.
    21	
    22	Formal architecture, plan, packaging, and specification QA evaluate the quality and readiness of their own artifacts. Global review remains advisory and must not issue a formal result.
    23	
    24	## Artifact QA Completeness Gate
    25	
    26	Before a formal artifact QA phase declares `PASS`, record:
    27	
    28	- Owner intent and governing sources reviewed: `<paths|missing>`.
    29	- DoD / phase acceptance criteria reviewed: `<yes|no>`.
    30	- Scope and out-of-scope consistency: `<aligned|partial|mismatch|unknown>`.
    31	- Artifact / relevant diff review: `<completed|incomplete>`.
    32	- Findings-first review: `<completed|incomplete>`.
    33	- Failure / rework / dependency scenarios: `<completed|not-applicable|incomplete>`.
    34	- Repository and source compatibility: `<aligned|partial|mismatch|unknown>`.
    35	- Post-fix full artifact re-review: `<completed|not-required|incomplete>`.
    36	- Evidence reviewed: `<paths|commands|manual checks>`.
    37	- Skipped or unreadable sources: `<none|list>`.
    38	- Residual risk: `<none|list>`.
    39	- Closure freshness: `<current|stale>`.
    40	
    41	Missing governing sources, an incomplete required review, a material mismatch, unresolved blocker, stale closure, or incomplete post-fix re-review means `FAIL` or a stop condition. A formal artifact QA result is valid only for that artifact and its next gate.
    42

     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	`Owner Decision Discovery` makes meaningful owner choices visible before dependent work begins. It asks about material decisions and owner preferences by default, while keeping repo-discoverable facts and small reversible implementation details out of the owner's way.
     6	
     7	This is a decision and interaction contract, not a new workflow phase. It does not grant write permission, change risk, replace evidence, approve a phase, or satisfy Definition of Done.
     8	
     9	## Decision Classes
    10	
    11	- `auto-resolvable`: low-impact, safe, reversible, inside accepted scope, and unlikely to change owner-visible outcomes; the agent may choose and must report it.
    12	- `owner-preference`: a meaningful choice about outcome, UX, presentation, tradeoff, client collaboration, or another owner preference; ask by default before dependent work.
    13	- `high-impact`: affects scope, architecture, data, integrations, cost, substantial rework, or long-lived behavior; owner decision is required.
    14	- `critical-risk`: uses the existing human-led approval and risk route; the agent must not resolve it.
    15	- `blocked-by-missing-facts`: required facts cannot be discovered from current sources and safe work cannot continue without them.
    16	
    17	Material decisions include scope/out-of-scope, DoD or acceptance criteria, owner-visible UX, architecture, data model, integrations, security, permissions, billing, migrations, production, real external effects, irreversible cost, and significant client or owner preferences.
    18	
    19	Formatting, local naming inside repository conventions, test file placement, and other low-impact reversible implementation details are normally `auto-resolvable` unless they materially affect the accepted outcome.
    20	
    21	## Discover Before Asking
    22	
    23	Before asking the owner:
    24	
    25	1. inspect current repository state, status, accepted artifacts, owner instructions, and available context;
    26	2. resolve discoverable facts from those sources;
    27	3. classify remaining choices;
    28	4. ask only when a real `owner-preference`, `high-impact`, `critical-risk`, or `blocked-by-missing-facts` decision remains.
    29	
    30	Do not ask the owner to locate a file, choose an existing convention, repeat a recorded decision, or provide a fact that can be discovered safely. Do not invent a question when no owner decision exists. Report `No owner decision needed` instead.

    33	
    34	Run Owner Decision Discovery after idea validation or batch triage and before dependent planning, specification, implementation, or another owner-sensitive write.
    35	
    36	For an interactive checkpoint:
    37	
    38	- group at most `1-3` questions that block the nearest safe next step;
    39	- put the recommended option first;
    40	- provide the reason the decision is needed now;
    41	- provide impact for the recommendation and each alternative;
    42	- provide `1-2` mutually exclusive alternatives when alternatives exist;

    44	- continue after the answer without asking again unless a new material decision appears.
    45	
    46	Do not ask generic permission such as `Should I continue?` when the owner already requested execution and no material decision remains.
    47

    53

    59	- alternatives and impacts;

**Finding — potential false positive in the trigger description.** The active [skill-creator description](/private/tmp/ai-workflow-skill-002-residual-001-safe/.systems/ai/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md:3) says to use it when work involves `SKILL.md` contracts. Narrowing that clause to work that **creates, adapts, reviews, evaluates, or packages a skill** would avoid the overlap. This is a wording-based risk; I did not run a trigger evaluation or observe an actual misroute.

I found no demonstrated missing route for this review in [Resource Routing](/private/tmp/ai-workflow-skill-002-residual-001-safe/.systems/ai/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md:62). No files were changed, and no formal phase gate ran.
